title: Source code escrow availability and deposit contents
status_rationale: No escrow arrangement, deposit or agreement exists. CNV-GOV-009 requires escrow or fork rights for noncommercial-licensed dependencies Unbound consumes; it does not commit Echelon to offer escrow to customers.
target_answer: Echelon offers a three-party escrow with an independent agent for customers that require it, with deposits that include the full source for Unbound and every Echelon library it depends on (for example Strata, Limen, Forma, Folio), build scripts and pinned dependency manifests with SBOM, database schema and migrations, infrastructure templates, operational runbooks and documentation sufficient for a competent .NET team. Deposits update automatically on every production release. A shared multi-beneficiary arrangement keeps cost low.
intended_practice: Decide whether to offer escrow or rely on alternatives (ANS-ESC-004); if offered, automate deposits from the release pipeline.
customer_statement: Echelon does not currently have a source code escrow arrangement. It is evaluating escrow and alternatives such as source-available licensing for customers that require continuity assurances.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC
open_questions: Which target customers require escrow as a condition of contract, and do they accept SaaS escrow including hosting and data, or only source?

challenge.customer_intent: Customer wants the service to continue if the vendor cannot provide it.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Vendor failure leaves the customer with no running system.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: For SaaS, source escrow alone is weak: releases are rare, deposits are often stale or unbuildable, and the customer lacks infrastructure, data and people to run the code.
challenge.contractually_required: Requested by some financial institutions and public-sector buyers.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Continuous customer-held data exports plus openly published schemas address data continuity without escrow.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Automated deposits on every release eliminate staleness if escrow is used.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Deposit receipts and verification results per release.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Source-available license with reproducible builds, plus customer-held data exports, may give stronger practical continuity than escrow.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes: reproducible builds can be checked by anyone with access.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If customers lack capability to operate F#/.NET and PostgreSQL systems, neither escrow nor source availability yields continuity.
challenge.conventional_cost: Low to medium (agent fees, verification fees).
challenge.alternative_risks: Source availability may expose security-sensitive code earlier.
supporting_arguments: Escrow deposits rarely enable real continuity for SaaS.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain: procurement checklists often name escrow specifically.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Procurement and examiners recognize escrow; alternatives require explanation.
Released code without the vendor's operational knowledge is still hard to run.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Escrow release conditions, license on release and practical usability
status_rationale: No escrow agreement exists, so no release conditions are defined.
target_answer: Release conditions include insolvency or bankruptcy filing, cessation of business, failure to remedy a material support failure within a defined cure period, discontinuation of the product, and assignment to an acquirer that does not assume obligations. On release the customer receives a perpetual license to use, modify and have a third party operate the code for its own and its donors' benefit. Echelon documents the skills and infrastructure needed to run the system and maintains a list of qualified operators.
intended_practice: Draft release conditions with counsel, including treatment in bankruptcy.
customer_statement: Echelon has no escrow agreement and therefore no release conditions to describe.

title: Escrow verification deposits and deposit protection
status_rationale: No escrow or verification exists. No reproducible build process for Unbound exists because Unbound is not built.
target_answer: Every deposit is verified automatically: an independent build environment reproduces the release from the deposit and compares artifact digests with production. Periodically an independent agent performs a full usability verification (build, deploy, load sample data, run smoke tests). Deposits are encrypted at rest at the agent, access is limited to release-authorized parties, and secrets are excluded and replaced with documented provisioning steps.
intended_practice: If escrow is offered, require automated build verification from the start.
customer_statement: Echelon has no escrow deposits or verification results.

title: Alternatives to escrow: source availability, reproducible builds, data and schema continuity, dependency continuity
status_rationale: CNV-GOV-009 requires that no production dependency be under a noncommercial license without a commercial license plus escrow or a fork right, and that dependencies be pinned with digests. SEC-SUPPLY-001 (proposed) requires locked versions, provenance and SBOM. Echelon's own libraries (Strata, Limen, Forma, Folio, Praxis) are separate repositories whose licenses are not recorded in the current-state brief.
target_answer: Continuity is provided by mechanisms customers can check at any time rather than at a release event: customer-held data exports with published schemas (ANS-TRM-003), reproducible builds with SLSA provenance and SBOMs for every release, source availability of Unbound and its Echelon libraries to customers under a license permitting continued operation if Echelon stops providing the service, and dependency continuity under CNV-GOV-009 so that no component the platform depends on can be withdrawn. Infrastructure templates and runbooks are included in what customers can access.
current_practice: Not established. CNV-GOV-009 is a requirement for dependencies only; no reproducible build, SLSA provenance or source-available license exists for Unbound.
intended_practice: Decide the license model for Unbound and Echelon libraries; implement reproducible builds and provenance in the release pipeline.
provable: Requirement text only: CNV-GOV-009 in unbound@9b38de47 and the proposed SEC-SUPPLY-001.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify commercial license plus escrow or fork rights for any noncommercial-licensed dependency and pinned, digest-verified dependency versions. Echelon has not yet decided whether to offer source availability to customers. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
